description: This image displays three pie charts, labeled "easy," "medium," and "hard," which appear to represent the distribution of different types of CoT (Chain-of-Thought) reasoning outcomes across three difficulty levels, as referenced in the paper "Knowledge Crosswords: Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language Models." Each pie chart is divided into four colored segments, corresponding to the categories N+K+ (teal), N−K+ (yellow), N−K− (orange), and N+K− (reddish-orange), as indicated by the shared legend on the right. The "easy" chart shows the largest segment as N−K+ at 45.9%, followed by N+K+ at 40.6%, then N+K− at 10.1%, and the smallest segment is N−K− at 3.3%. The "medium" chart has the largest segment as N−K+ at 44.3%, followed by N+K+ at 44.6%, then N+K− at 7.2%, and the smallest is N−K− at 3.9%. The "hard" chart shows the largest segment as N−K− at 36.8%, followed by N−K+ at 36.2%, then N+K+ at 20.1%, and the smallest is N+K− at 7.0%. All percentage values are labeled directly within their respective slices, and the segments are arranged in descending order of size within each chart.
